title: Spotter's Challenge
scoring: 3 points for a first-try answer, 2 for second, 1 for third, 0 if missed.
note: TEST build: answers are in this file. The live version should check answers server-side (see LEADERBOARD-PLAN.md).

puzzles.question: Which exact 777 variant is this?
clues: Start with the wingtip, then count the door pairs.
It has the GE90-115B, the only engine offered on this variant.
The best-selling 777 version by far, and a daily sight at LAX.
puzzles.tell: Raked wingtips plus the long fuselage with five door pairs. The -300 has the same length but no raked tips; the -200LR has raked tips but only four door pairs.
puzzles.fact: United 777-300ER on final at Washington Dulles. Registration and fleet number blurred so you cannot look it up.

puzzles.question: Name the engine on this 747.
clues: Look at the trailing edge of the fan nozzle.
Only one 747 version could have this engine, and it first flew in 2010.
A bleed-air sibling of one of the 787's two engine choices.
puzzles.tell: Chevrons (the sawtooth trailing edge) on the nacelle. Of the 747's engine options, only the 747-8's GEnx-2B has them; CF6, PW4000 and RB211 nacelles have smooth edges.
puzzles.fact: Nippon Cargo Airlines 747-8F JA13KZ on approach to Tokyo Narita. The engine name printed on the nacelles is blurred.

puzzles.question: Which SoCal airport is this?
clues: The building opened in 1941 and is a protected landmark.
The control tower sits on top of the terminal itself.
Its runway 30 is the longest on the field and its airline slots are capped by a local noise ordinance.
puzzles.tell: The 1941 Streamline Moderne terminal with its rooftop tower and porthole windows. Burbank's terminal is a 1930 Spanish Revival building and ONT and SBA have modern terminals.
puzzles.fact: Long Beach's historic terminal now serves as the ticketing building; gates are in the newer concourse behind it. The airport name on the facade is blurred.

puzzles.question: Exact 737 variant? Type it in.
clues: Count the exits behind the wing.
LEAP-1B engines with chevroned nacelles and split-tip winglets.
Longer than the -8, shorter than the -10.
puzzles.tell: The mid-cabin exit door (a plugged door on Alaska's jets) just behind the wing. The 737-8 does not have it; the 737-900ER has it too but has CFM56 engines with smooth nacelles and no split-tip winglets.
puzzles.fact: Alaska Airlines 737-9 departing Boston runway 33L. Registration blurred.

puzzles.question: This 747 later became NASA 905. Who was its first operator?
clues: It is a 747-100, delivered new in 1970.
Boeing's customer code in its model number is 23.
Its original registration was N9668.
puzzles.tell: The model number. NASA 905 is a 747-123, and the '23' customer code belongs to American Airlines. NASA bought it in 1974.
puzzles.fact: In September 2012 NASA 905 carried Space Shuttle Endeavour on its final ferry flight into LAX, with a low pass over SoCal on the way.

puzzles.question: Close-up of the main gear. Which aircraft?
clues: Count the wheels on one main gear leg.
Airbus stretched this one by about 7 m and gave it a stronger gear.
Launch operator was Qatar Airways in 2018.
puzzles.tell: Six-wheel main bogies. The A350-900, A330neo and 787-10 all use four-wheel bogies.
puzzles.fact: This photo shows the first A350-1000 delivered. Launch customer Qatar Airways took it in February 2018.

puzzles.question: Three of these jets had their final assembly in Southern California. Which one did not?
clues: The TriStar in the photo is one of the three.
Think Long Beach and Palmdale.
The odd one out was built alongside the 737 in Washington state.
puzzles.tell: The 757 came off Boeing's Renton, Washington line. TriStars were assembled at Lockheed's Palmdale plant; the MD-11 and 717 at Douglas (later Boeing) Long Beach.
puzzles.fact: The last airliner built in Long Beach was a 717 for AirTran in 2006; the C-17 line there closed in 2015.

puzzles.question: Which exact variant is this airBaltic jet?
clues: Judge the cabin length against the size of the engines.
airBaltic's entire jet fleet is a single type and a single length.
It is the longer of the two versions Bombardier designed as the CSeries.
puzzles.tell: The big PW1500G geared turbofans under a clean, slim wing and the long cabin. The A220-300 is 3.7 m longer than the -100, the E195-E2 has a different nose and tail, and the A319neo has wingtip sharklets.
puzzles.fact: airBaltic flies only the A220-300 and was its launch operator in December 2016, when the type was still called the Bombardier CS300. Registration blurred.

puzzles.question: Name the engine family on this Cathay Pacific A330-300.
clues: Rule out the A330neo-only option first.
Cathay picked the British option for every A330 it ordered.
Cathay Pacific was the launch operator of this engine in 1995.
puzzles.tell: This is an A330ceo, so the neo-only Trent 7000 is out, and Cathay Pacific specified the Trent 700 for all of its A330s. Expert spotters also look for the Trent's long, full-length nacelle.
puzzles.fact: The Trent 700 entered service with Cathay Pacific on the A330 in 1995, the first member of the Trent family to fly with an airline.

puzzles.question: Which Southern California airport terminal is this?
clues: Read the landscape, not the building.
Low desert scrub, palms and bare mountains close behind the field.
It sits at the foot of Mount San Jacinto, with open-air gate areas on the ramp.
puzzles.tell: The white tent-style canopies over the terminal plus the open Coachella Valley desert and mountains right behind it. ONT and BUR sit in built-up valleys, and SAN is on San Diego Bay.
puzzles.fact: Palm Springs International is the main airline airport for the Coachella Valley. Its original terminal was designed by desert modernist architect Donald Wexler and opened in 1965.

puzzles.question: Exact 787 variant? Type it in.
clues: Compare the cabin length behind the wing to the length ahead of it.
The longest Dreamliner, a simple stretch of the -9.
United is its largest US operator and Singapore Airlines took the first one.
puzzles.tell: A very long, slender fuselage with an extra-long aft cabin. The 787-10 is 5.5 m longer than the -9 and 11.6 m longer than the -8, with the same wing.
puzzles.fact: The 787-10 first flew in March 2017 and entered service with Singapore Airlines in April 2018. Registration, fleet number and the 787 lettering are blurred.

puzzles.question: This NASA 747SP flying observatory was based in Palmdale. Who was its first operator?
clues: It was delivered new in 1977.
Its first owner named it Clipper Lindbergh.
It later flew for United before NASA bought it.
puzzles.tell: SOFIA (N747NA) began life with Pan Am as Clipper Lindbergh, moved to United when Pan Am sold its Pacific routes, and was bought by NASA in 1997.
puzzles.fact: SOFIA carried a 2.5 m infrared telescope behind a door in its rear fuselage. It flew its last science mission in 2022 and is now displayed at the Pima Air and Space Museum in Tucson.

puzzles.question: Which exact variant is this narrowbody?
clues: Count the doors and look how far the fuselage runs behind the wing.
Only 55 of this version were built.
Launch customer was the German leisure airline Condor in 1999.
puzzles.tell: A 757 wing and nose, but a far longer fuselage stretching well behind the wing. The 757-300 is about 7 m longer than the -200, which makes it the longest single-aisle twin jet built.
puzzles.fact: Delta inherited its 757-300s from Northwest. Registration and fleet numbers blurred.

puzzles.question: The jet in the photo is an MD-88. Three of these types are members of its DC-9 family. Which is the odd one out?
clues: Rear-mounted engines and a T-tail are not enough to decide.
Three were built by Douglas (later McDonnell Douglas and Boeing) in Long Beach.
The odd one out came from the Netherlands.
puzzles.tell: The Fokker 100 grew out of the Dutch Fokker F28. The 717 (launched as the MD-95), MD-87 and MD-90 are all DC-9 derivatives built in Long Beach.
puzzles.fact: Delta retired its last MD-88s in June 2020. Registration too small to read in this photo.
